Probe_A_WeightNorm_vs_Recall.description: Correlation between class head L2 norm and per-class OOF Balanced Accuracy / Recall

Probe_B_CosineSim_vs_ConfusionRate.description: Correlation between class head cosine similarity and empirical confusion rate (153 pairs)

Probe_C_FoldDrift_vs_FoldBA.description: Correlation between fold head distance to full-fit and fold Balanced Accuracy (5 folds)

Probe_D_Summary.finding: High cosine similarity in weight space directly explains 73.8% of variance in same-family confusion rates, but does NOT reliably differentiate subtle intra-family sibling pairs (where weight vectors have near-identical cosine alignment > 0.82).

depth_specialization.depth_with_highest_discriminative_power: Depth 6 (Layer 22) and Depth 7 (Layer 27) account for >45% of total classification weight norm across all 18 classes.
depth_specialization.depth_with_lowest_weight_norm: Depth 0 (Layer 2) and Depth 1 (Layer 4) carry <12% of total weight norm, primarily encoding generic syntax rather than LLM identity.

top_parameter_blocks.gate_proj_MLP: Largest update norm (mean 23.56) and spectral norm (23.21); 86.2% rank-1 dominance.
top_parameter_blocks.layer_27_readout: Final pooled depth carries 18.5% of total weight norm for all 18 classes.
top_parameter_blocks.layer_4_gemini_discriminator: Separates Gemini 3.7 vs 3.8 Flash (accounting for 97 mutual errors).

statistically_significant_correlations.name: Class Head Weight Norm vs OOF Recall
statistically_significant_correlations.interpretation: Under-represented or frequently confused classes suffer from suppressed weight norms (norm ~7.5 vs ~9.4), causing systemic under-prediction under standard argmax.

statistically_significant_correlations.name: Weight Vector Cosine Similarity vs Confusion Probability
statistically_significant_correlations.interpretation: High cosine alignment in weight space directly explains mutual confusion rate across the 153 class pairs.

candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.mechanism: Class weight norms vary from 7.53 (GLM-5.3) to 9.43 (GPT-6 Astra). Normalizing class weight vectors to uniform unit norm (or class-specific temperature scaling) removes the norm suppression bias.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.predicted_change: Increases recall for low-norm classes (GLM-5.3, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Fable) without retraining.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.falsification_experiment: Unit-normalize W_plain rows and evaluate on prompt-disjoint OOF. If Balanced Accuracy drops, hypothesis is falsified.

candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.mechanism: Gemini 3.7 vs 3.8 Flash are collinear in overall weight space (cos=0.88), but show peak separation in Depth 1 (Layer 4). Boosting Layer 4 weights relative to Layer 27 for the Gemini family resolves sibling confusion.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.predicted_change: Resolves the 97 mutual errors between Gemini 3.7 and 3.8 Flash.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.falsification_experiment: Apply depth-specific scaling to Gemini logits and measure intra-family Balanced Accuracy on OOF.

candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.mechanism: Gate projection LoRA updates are overwhelmingly rank-1 (86.2% variance on sigma_1) across all layers, acting as an isotropic gating amplifier rather than model-specific attribution feature.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.predicted_change: Truncating gate_proj to rank 1 or zeroing out trailing singular components will preserve attribution accuracy while reducing noise.
candidate_hypotheses_and_edits.falsification_experiment: Singular value truncation of gate_proj LoRA matrices.
